# Intake brief — Explosions should be explosions (image-based explosion VFX)

> **Source request (verbatim):** "The explosions right now are just multiple
> circles. They look OK but we can improve them a great deal. Make them actual
> explosion images that change shape as they shrink. Each should be a subtle
> variation on the red/orange explosion colour."

## Problem statement

Every destruction burst is still rendered as a cloud of small filled circles,
so explosions read as "a lot of dots" rather than as an explosion. Replace the
circle particles with image-based explosion shapes whose silhouette changes as
they shrink and fade, tinted from a red/orange fire palette with subtle
per-particle variation.

## Users

- **Player** — the primary user; perceives destruction feedback.
  - *As a player, when I destroy an enemy or lose my ship, I see a recognisable
    explosion (a hot core, ragged flame lobes, sparks) rather than a spray of
    dots, so combat impact feels real and satisfying.*
- **Developer / designer** — tunes the look without touching gameplay code.
  - *As a developer, I can adjust the fire palette, frame count, morph timing
    and particle counts through named exported constants in one shared module
    and verify the behaviour deterministically in unit tests.*
- **Agent / maintainer** — must be able to change the look once.
  - *As a maintainer, I know the game and every gym consume the same VFX code,
    so a look change cannot drift between the game and the gym scenes.*

## Decisions pending producer confirmation

These three questions materially change the implementation and are recorded as
**OPEN QUESTION** entries in the Appendix. The ACs below assume the
**recommended** option for each, so the brief is implementable as written if the
producer accepts all recommendations.

1. **Art source** — procedural runtime-generated explosion textures
   (**recommended**) vs. committed raster sprite sheets vs. Graphics-only
   morphing polygons.
2. **Colour policy** — all explosions move to a red/orange fire palette
   (**recommended**) vs. keep the current per-entity hue and add a hot
   red/orange core vs. red/orange for enemy deaths only.
3. **Coverage** — every `spawnExplosionParticles` call site (**recommended**:
   enemy/boss/player deaths, victory fireworks, wave-timeout penalty, gyms) vs.
   entity-death bursts only.

## Existing state

- All destruction VFX route through one shared module,
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` (`spawnExplosionParticles()`), used by
  `BaseEnemy`, `Boss`, `CombatCoreScene._spawnPlayerExplosion`,
  `playerDeathJuice`, `endOfRunJuice` (victory fireworks/defeat) and the gyms
  (via the shared combat core), so game↔gym parity already holds.
- A burst is a **single Phaser `Graphics`** animated by one tween; each frame
  redraws every live particle as `fillCircle(p.x, p.y, p.radius)` with a
  colour from `jitterColor(baseColor)` (HSL jitter ±`EXPLOSION_HUE_JITTER_DEG`
  = 20° around the exploding entity's palette colour). Particles fade
  (`1 - fadeStep·elapsed`) and shrink over `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS` (400 ms).
- Three patterns exist (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`) mapped per entity in
  `EXPLOSION_PATTERNS_BY_TYPE`; counts scale with entity size (clamped 8–80).
- Determinism: all jitter is drawn from a seeded PRNG (`createRng(seed)`), and
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` pins geometry, colour bands, counts,
  jitter and the Phaser integration through a structural scene double.
- Live per-kind counts are exposed by `getExplosionVfxCounts()` /
  `resetExplosionVfxCounts()` and consumed by the action-intensity metric.
- The repo ships **no image assets** today: `public/` contains only audio
  (`public/audio/sfx/*.wav`); every other visual is drawn procedurally
  (Graphics / shapes). Audio assets are baked from ToneForge recipes by
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Documentation of the current circle rendering lives in
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.1–§7.2 (particle-effects and
  explosion-patterns bullets) and `README.md` ("Explosion VFX (particle
  bursts)").

## Desired change

1. Replace circle particles with **explosion imagery**: a small set of
   explosion shapes (e.g. 4–6 frames per burst family) whose silhouette changes
   over the burst's life as the particle shrinks and fades, so the explosion
   visibly *evolves* (hot dense core → ragged flame lobes → thin embers)
   instead of uniformly shrinking dots.
2. Use a **red/orange fire palette** with subtle variation per particle
   (hue/lightness jitter inside a constrained warm band, plus a brighter
   white-hot core), rather than the current entity-hue tinting.
3. Keep the existing pattern system (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`), counts,
   lifespan, seeded determinism, teardown/registry contract and per-kind
   counters intact — this is a rendering/feel change, not a gameplay change.
4. Apply the change through the single shared module so the game and every gym
   get it automatically (no divergent copies).

## Acceptance Criteria

> AC1–AC3 depend on the recommended decisions (procedural textures, red/orange
> palette, all call sites). If the producer chooses another option, the ACs are
> revised before implementation.

- [ ] **AC1 — Explosion imagery replaces circles.** `spawnExplosionParticles()`
  renders each particle as an explosion shape from a cached, shared texture/frame
  set (no per-frame `fillCircle` particle rendering); a burst visibly reads as a
  blast (core + lobes/embers), not as a cloud of circles.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shape changes as the particle shrinks.** Each particle's shape
  frame is a deterministic function of its normalised age, so the silhouette
  morphs through at least 3 distinct frames from spawn to expiry while the
  particle also scales/shrinks; the final state is a thin ember, not a dot.
- [ ] **AC3 — Red/orange fire palette with subtle variation.** All explosion
  colours derive from exported warm-palette constants; 100% of emitted particle
  colours fall inside the documented red/orange hue band with bounded
  saturation/lightness variance (asserted across every colour the module emits,
  including cores, for both death bursts and victory fireworks).
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour preserved.** Pattern assignment, size-scaled counts
  (8–80), `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS`, seeded reproducibility (same seed ⇒ identical
  frames/colours/positions), the `opts.registry` teardown contract, the
  `getExplosionVfxCounts()` increments/decrements, the `delay`/`depth`/`scale`
  options and the null-scene guard all behave exactly as before.
- [ ] **AC5 — Single shared implementation / parity.** The change lives only in
  the shared VFX module (+ its texture helper); the game and every gym use it
  with no duplicated rendering code, and the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and gym-parity docs
  assertions still pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Deterministic, headless-testable tests.** Unit tests cover frame
  selection/morph progression, colour-band invariants, determinism, teardown and
  counters without a real WebGL canvas (texture provider is injectable/stubbable
  and preserves the existing structural scene double), and an in-game/gym visual
  verification is documented (GymFodderEnemies death bursts, player death,
  victory fireworks).
- [ ] **AC7 — Performance budget.** Concurrency stays bounded: no per-particle
  texture generation, frame textures are generated once and reused, and no
  regression in particle counts or teardown (no leaked display objects after
  scene SHUTDOWN/restart).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation updated.** GDD §7.1–§7.2 (particle effects,
  explosion-patterns/colour table), the README "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)"
  section and the module header/comments describe the image-based look, palette
  and frame/morph constants, replacing the "small filled circles",
  "Hues stay recognisably 'that ship'", and per-entity colour statements.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependency**; stay on Phaser primitives.
- **Zero-asset repo convention** (recommended option): generate the explosion
  textures at runtime from code, cached by key; do not commit binary art unless
  the producer chooses the sprite-sheet option.
- **GDD §7.1 style rule**: "Geometric, angular shapes … No organic forms".
  Literal photographic/smoke-puff explosion images would conflict; the
  recommended look is a stylised neon blast (angular/ragged polygon lobes) to
  stay within the established art language — the producer may override.
- **Gym↔game parity** (repo convention / AGENTS.md): one shared code path.
- **Determinism**: seeded PRNG only; no `Math.random()` in VFX.
- **Performance**: bursts can be dense (Boss layers 3 patterns, victory
  fireworks up to 30 staggered bursts); textured particles must not multiply
  draw calls per particle in a way that breaks the current action-intensity
  budget. Use shared textures + batched images, and keep the existing count
  clamps.
- **Scope discipline**: gameplay numbers (damage, counts, timing, SFX) are out
  of scope; extra ideas are recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — replace the Graphics circle renderer with a
  pre-generated/cached explosion frame texture provider and per-particle
  image/quad rendering whose frame is a function of normalised age; add the
  warm-palette constants + colour resolution; keep the pure geometry/PRNG,
  pattern, lifecycle, registry and counter contracts.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` — extend/extend-and-rename the pure-state
  and Phaser-double tests for frames, morph progression, colour band,
  determinism, teardown and counters.
- `src/vfx/explosionTextures.ts` (new, predicted) — procedural frame generation
  (deterministic polygon/blob silhouettes per frame) plus the texture cache/
  keyed registry and a headless-safe seam.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — the warm fire palette constants (or keep them in the
  VFX module, following the module's existing constant-export convention).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.1–§7.2 particle-effects and explosion
  pattern/colour text.
- `README.md` — "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)" section.
- Call sites that need no code change but must be visually verified:
  `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
  `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` (victory fireworks).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ambiguity risk** — the colour request may mean "keep ship identity but make
  the blast feel fiery". If the producer picks the recommended full red/orange
  palette, per-entity identity (Scout green, Diver yellow, Phaser magenta,
  player cyan) is intentionally lost and the GDD tables must change; this is
  recorded as an explicit assumption rather than silently decided.
- **GDD style conflict risk** — "no organic forms" vs. explosion images; the
  recommended stylised-neon-blast silhouette keeps the language, but a producer
  preference for realistic puffs would require an art pipeline.
- **Performance risk** — replacing one Graphics with N images per burst could
  regress frame time in dense scenes (Boss + fireworks). Mitigation: shared
  cached textures, a bounded texture count, batched rendering, and a check of
  the action-intensity/perf capture before review.
- **Test harness risk** — texture generation needs a canvas; the recommended
  procedural option must expose an injectable provider so headless Vitest runs
  stay deterministic and do not need WebGL.
- **Scope-creep risk** — tempting extras (screen-shake per particle, heat
  distortion, sound layering, per-entity explosion image families) are recorded
  as linked follow-up items, not added here.
- **Assumption** — the operator's "each should be a subtle variation on the
  red/orange explosion colour" refers to per-particle colour variation inside a
  warm palette, not a single flat orange.

## Related work

- **Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths**
  (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — the parent feature that introduced the circle-based
  particle bursts this item replaces visually.
- **Explosion pattern emitters and combinator** (AH-0MTVID632005ACBF) —
  `radial`/`ring`/`implosion` geometry that must be preserved.
- **Explosion particle test suite** (AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ) — the test-first
  contract this change must extend rather than break.
- **Entity-centred explosion colour jitter** (AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034) — the
  per-entity hue jitter explicitly superseded by the new warm palette.
- **Add randomness to explosion** (AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH) — seeded size/position
  jitter that must remain deterministic.
- **Parity: gym↔game verification + explosion registry** (AH-0MUZQGRQR0086NP6)
  — the per-kind counter and parity guards that this change must keep green.
- **Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory** (AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44) and
  **Explosions timed with the beat** (AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3) — other consumers of
  `spawnExplosionParticles` whose look/behaviour must stay coherent.
- Related docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.1–§7.2, `README.md`
  (Explosion VFX), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.5 gym surface),
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` (VFX counters).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V** – Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths (completed)
- **AH-0MTVID632005ACBF** – Explosion pattern emitters and combinator (completed)
- **AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ** – Explosion particle test suite (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.1–§7.2 explosion VFX/particle docs
- `README.md` — "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)" section
- `CHANGELOG.md` — release history

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answers are pending; this intake stopped at the producer-review gate. Each entry
is an **OPEN QUESTION** with the agent's recommended option. Update in place
(never duplicate) when answers arrive.

- **Q1 (art source).** How should the explosion imagery be produced?
  (a) Procedurally generated at runtime into cached Phaser textures — keeps the
  repo's zero-asset convention and determinism; (b) committed raster sprite
  sheets/atlases under `public/` — needs an art source and an asset pipeline;
  (c) Graphics-only morphing polygons — lightest, but not really "images".
  **Recommended:** (a) — the repo ships no image assets, all VFX are code-drawn,
  and this keeps the seeded/deterministic test contract and gym↔game parity
  intact.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q2 (colour policy).** Should explosions drop the per-entity hue (Scout green,
  Diver yellow, Tank orange, Phaser magenta, Swarm blue, Boss red, player cyan)
  in favour of a red/orange fire palette with subtle per-particle variation?
  (a) Yes, every explosion becomes red/orange variants; (b) keep the entity hue
  as the base but add a red/orange hot core; (c) red/orange for enemy-death
  bursts only, keep player cyan and multi-colour victory fireworks.
  **Recommended:** (a) — matches the operator's wording ("subtle variation on
  the red/orange explosion colour") and the "explosions should look like
  explosions" intent; note this intentionally supersedes AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q3 (coverage).** Which burst sites adopt the new look? (a) All
  `spawnExplosionParticles` call sites — enemy/boss/player deaths, victory
  fireworks, wave-timeout penalty and every gym; (b) entity-death explosions
  only; (c) entity + player death only.
  **Recommended:** (a) — one shared implementation keeps gym↔game parity and
  avoids two explosion looks in one frame.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q4 (implicit, answered by repo research).** Do gym scenes need separate
  wiring? — Answer (agent research): No; gyms reach the VFX through the shared
  combat core and `spawnExplosionParticles`, so the change propagates
  automatically. Evidence: `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule.
- **Q5 (implicit, answered by repo research).** Is there an existing image asset
  pipeline to reuse? — Answer (agent research): No; `public/` contains only
  baked audio and the menu's GitHub data-URI SVG. Evidence: `public/` tree,
  `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`, `scripts/build-audio.sh`.

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

# Intake brief — Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)

## Headline

Replace the mini-boss reward choice with a **spin-the-wheel** that always
delivers a guaranteed permanent upgrade: one bonus slot upgrades everything,
5 slots upgrade 3 picks, 10 upgrade 2, and the remaining 84 upgrade 1 — so a
mini-boss victory always makes the build meaningfully stronger.

## Problem statement

Mini-boss rewards currently offer a flat menu (upgrade any one owned item, or
unlock one locked weapon) which reads as a low-value chore rather than a
reward. The player wants a moment of anticipation that *always* pays out in
power, presented as a wheel of fortune spin over the power-ups the player has
invested in permanent slots.

## Users

- **Player (core loop):** after defeating a mini-boss, expects a celebration
  and a guaranteed, tangible power gain.
- **Demo/attract bot:** must not stall on the wheel; auto-spins after the same
  human-like delay as the hold-full choice (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F contract).

### Example user story

> As a player, when I defeat a mini-boss, I want to click a button to spin a
> wheel showing the power-ups in my permanent slots, watch it slow to a stop,
> and receive the landed upgrade(s) — so the reward feels like a gamble that
> always pays out, not a to-do list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Defeating a mini-boss opens a **wheel overlay** (the multi-option upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone): one wedge per **owned permanent kind** across the shared six-slot pool — power-up kinds **and** weapon drops — plus a single **bonus** wedge; play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice.
- Spinning is player-initiated (click/keyboard), the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (building tension; the outcome must not be predictable until it stops), and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.
- The spin outcome follows the **100-slot distribution**: 1 slot = bonus (every owned permanent kind +1 level), 5 slots = 3 upgrades, 10 slots = 2 upgrades, 84 slots = 1 upgrade. Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct** owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count (a player with one owned power-up landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
- The run-scoped weapon-unlock feature and its reward options are **removed** from mini-boss rewards (locked-pool option builders, `getUnlockedWeapons` and the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field; `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bumped so stale checkpoints are rejected cleanly).
- Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (no `Math.random()`), the distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the game and gyms both consume, and demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md`, checkpoint notes), including code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, including unit tests for the slot distribution/outcome resolver and PlayScene wheel-flow tests replacing the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): slot distribution and reward
  application must live once in shared modules consumed by `PlayScene` and any
  gym surface; no scene-private divergence.
- **Code-first visuals:** icons come from the existing code-drawn
  `src/powerups/icons.ts` (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets (GDD §7.2).
- **Seed reproducibility:** run-seeded RNG only; deterministic tests.
- **Launcher-agnostic overlay:** a single optional selection/result callback
  (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s `onSelect`), so any launcher can drive it.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation (test-slot policy); changed
  scope is run via the test skill.

## Existing state

- Defeating a mini-boss fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` → `openMiniBossReward`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), which offers **one** upgrade-or-unlock choice:
  every owned permanent weapon/power-up level-up offer (built by
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`) plus every still-locked weapon from
  `MINI_BOSS_LOCKED_WEAPONS` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`). The overlay is the
  shared `MineralChoiceScene`; selection applies `applyMineralChoiceReward`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`, re-exported by
  `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`). Rewards are applied exactly once
  (`selectMiniBossReward` resets the open flag). See GDD §4.4.4
  (AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH).
- **Note (stale description):** the description's "choice of 5 random power
  ups" does not match current behaviour — the live reward is the
  upgrade-or-unlock menu described above; the wheel replaces *that*.
- Each wheel-relevant decision is a permanent kind in a **shared 6-slot pool**
  (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) covering both power-up kinds and weapon drops;
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks permanent vs
  temporary levels and per-kind caps; the checkpoint
  (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) persists weapon/power-up levels and
  `unlockedWeapons` (the latter is removed by AC5).
- Demo mode already auto-selects the reward via `_randomDemoRewardIndex()`
  after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) — reuse this
  seam for auto-spin.

## Desired change

- New pure module (e.g. `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`): the 100-slot
  distribution (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single), a weighted
  outcome resolver over owned permanent kinds, distinct-kind multi-upgrade
  selection (repeats only when fewer kinds than picks), cap-aware handling,
  injectable RNG.
- New launcher-agnostic overlay (e.g. `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`): one
  wedge per owned icon plus the bonus wedge, pointer, fast-starting/eased-out
  spin, landed-wedge highlight, click/keyboard to spin, result callback.
  Register in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward`: launch the
  wheel with the owned permanent kinds (from `resolveSlotState`/
  `getWeaponLevels`/`getPowerUpLevels`), apply the resolved outcome once
  through the shared reward machinery, fall back to the three-option choice
  when nothing is owned, and keep demo auto-spin.
- Remove the unlock feature (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts` locked-pool state and
  option builders, `PlayScene.getUnlockedWeapons`, the checkpoint
  `unlockedWeapons` field) and bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- Update GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` and checkpoint docs.
- Replace the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests in
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; add deterministic unit tests for the
  distribution and outcome resolver.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — rework `openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward` to the wheel flow; fallback; demo auto-spin; drop unlock state.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new) — pure 100-slot distribution + weighted outcome resolver, distinct-kind picks, caps.
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new) — launcher-agnostic wheel overlay: wedges, spin + ease-out animation, pointer, result callback.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — reuse `drawPowerUpIcon`/`drawWeaponIcon` for wheel wedges.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — owned permanent kinds feeding the wheel population.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — unlock machinery to be removed (AC5).
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` / `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — shared reward application for spin outcomes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register the wheel scene.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — remove `unlockedWeapons`; bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — exercise the shared wheel/reward path (parity).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (new) — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool (current behaviour being replaced).
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — AI bot reward-screen selection (demo auto-select contract to preserve).
- AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF — six-slot permanent loadout accounting (slot pool the wheel reads).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level store (permanent levels/caps applied by the wheel).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (shared modules requirement).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice overlay (pattern the wheel scene mirrors).

- AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD — Mini-boss/boss strength scales with player firepower (completed; adjacent balance context for reward power).
- AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y — Show current upgrades on the hull-full screen (open; same "player must see what they own" UI concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk:** celebration VFX/audio for the spin and rebalancing the
  1/5/10/84 split are follow-ups — record as separate work items, not scope.
- **Assumption (cap-aware draws):** when a drawn kind has hit its level cap,
  re-draw a non-capped owned kind; if every owned kind is capped the spin
  grants a fallback (minerals). Confirm during planning.
- **Assumption (mandatory spin):** the wheel always grants something and has
  no skip/decline path (a refusable "reward" recreates the perceived-nothing
  outcome).
- **Risk (unlock removal):** deleting the unlock feature removes a shipped
  progression mechanic; GDD §4.4.4 and the locked-pool docs must be rewritten
  in the same change so no doc promises unlocks. `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bump
  invalidates existing checkpoints (accepted: pre-release).
- **Risk (resolver/UI drift):** the wedge list and the weighted outcome must
  be derived from the same owned-kind snapshot; the scene must never compute
  probabilities itself.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of unlock rewards.** "The wheel shows icons of power-ups the

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want an executable contract (failing tests) for the two level-scaling axes before any production code exists, so the curves, rounding rules and cap behaviour are pinned before implementation.

This is the test-first item for the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` module and the `GameRules` scaling data (AC "Data-driven level-scaling curves" and the unit-test part of AC "Tests" of the parent item AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Create `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new file) and extend `src/core/rules.test.ts` with tests that pin the agreed contract. These tests must **fail on pre-change HEAD** because neither the module nor the rules fields exist yet.

Curve contract to pin:

- `enemyCountMultiplier(level)`: `1.0` at level 1, `2.0` at level 10, linear in between (assert the exact formula value at level 5, e.g. `1 + (level - 1) * (1.0 / 9)`), monotonically non-decreasing across 1–10.
- `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)`: `0.18` at level 1 (equal to the exported `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`), `0.05` at level 10, monotonically non-increasing across 1–10, and `chance(10) <= 0.3 * chance(1)`.
- Extra Life proportionality: the small-asteroid Extra Life chance scales by the same ratio as the per-kill chance (`chance(level) / chance(1)`), so level 1 equals `rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` exactly.
- Input clamping: levels below 1 clamp to 1, levels above the campaign maximum clamp to the maximum, and non-finite/non-integer inputs resolve to a documented clamped integer (no `NaN` output).
- Count application helper (`applyEnemyCountScaling` or the agreed equivalent): documented round-half-up rule, floor of 1, per-group safety cap of 200, `single`-formation groups left at exactly 1, and a level-1 identity transform (deep-equal input/output).
- Rules: the new scaling fields have documented defaults (1.0→2.0 multiplier, 0.18→0.05 drop chance), are clamped on load, and a legacy persisted blob without them loads with the defaults merged (backwards-compatible, no schema break).

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests exist and fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (module/rules fields absent); record the failure output in a comment on this item.
- Tests cover monotonicity, clamping, level-1 identity, rounding rule, `single` groups, the 200 cap, Extra Life proportionality and legacy rules-blob merging.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).
- Every test name states the behaviour it pins; no asserts without a stated reason.

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Tests** — Unit tests cover curve monotonicity/clamping, count application (rounding, `single` groups, caps, L1 identity, seeded determinism), per-level drop chance, Extra Life proportionality and game↔gym parity. New tests fail on the pre-change code and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the level-scaling implementation item.

# Bot should be aware of screen wrap around (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG)

## Problem statement

The game's playfield is a wrap-around (torus) arena — the player ship, asteroids,
bullets and raider patrol all cross a screen edge and reappear on the opposite
side — but the AI bot's decision layer (`src/ai/`) is wrap-blind: it treats the
four bounding edges as solid walls it must not approach, never crosses a seam on
purpose, and measures every distance, bearing, aim solution, threat prediction
and nearest-selection along the raw (unwrapped) straight line. A human player
routinely uses the seam to chase, flee and angle shots; the bot cannot, so demo
play looks unhuman, the bot camps near the walls it wrongly fears, and it
systematically misjudges everything on the far side of an edge.

## Users

- **Players / viewers of the attract demo** — the demo bot is deliberately
  human-like (human reaction cadence, W/A/D controls, thrust feel); humans use
  the wrap, so a bot that refuses to is conspicuous.
- **Developers** — one coherent torus model in the decision layer, so future
  features (seam-aware enemy fire, new archetypes, tuning) share a single
  implementation instead of adding seam hacks.

### Example user stories

- As a **player watching the demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge to
  reach a target that is closer the other way, so its movement looks like a
  human's.
- As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
  shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite
  edge — so engagements play out in the whole wrap-around arena.
- As a **player**, I want the bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
  across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming.
- As a **developer**, I want one wrap-aware geometry implementation used by
  steering, aim, prediction and distance, so the model is consistent and
  testable, and the headless eval measures the same physics the bot faces in
  the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wrap-aware steering (movement)** — The four arena edges stop being walls in
   the steering safety/clearance test: both the legacy `evaluateVector`
   (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) and the competent `evaluateDirection`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) no longer reject a direction
   solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`, and steering toward an
   objective uses the **shortest wrapped path** (the closer of the raw bearing
   and the seam-crossing bearing to the objective's opposite-edge duplicate) so
   the bot crosses an edge to get to the other side — used deliberately when
   net-positive (Q2), never as a scripted trick. Unit tests cover each of the
   four edges: the wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter; an
   edge-crossing direction is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.

2. **Seam-aware aim & targeting** — Aim and target selection run on the torus:
   `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the
   shortest wrapped path, and `nearestTarget` / `nearestEnemyDistance` choose
   nearest by wrapped distance. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or
   mineral is shorter than the raw line, the bot points at the seam duplicate —
   firing off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge. Tests assert the aim
   angle equals the wrapped-path angle when that route is shorter, and that
   behaviour is unchanged when the raw line is already shortest.

3. **Seam-aware threat & hazard prediction** — `predictIncomingFire`
   (`worldModel.ts`), the competent `closestApproach` solves and the legacy
   path-crossing checks operate on the wrapped torus, so shots and moving
   hazards whose closest approach to the player crosses a seam are predicted and
   dodged. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's existing wrap-jump clamp is
   re-verified so it does not double-compensate once positions are modelled on
   the torus. Tests: a seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening (a
   raw-line-only view would miss it).

4. **`wallMargin` retired cleanly** — The now-meaningless wall-margin tunable is
   retired (or demonstrably re-purposed) across `botDecision.ts`,
   `competent/tunables.ts`, `style/fitting.ts` and `tuningFields.ts`; saved
   bot-tuning configs (`src/data/bot-tuning.json` and any gym-saved tunings)
   still load with the field gone (unknown-field tolerance), and the style-fit
   mapping is updated per the retirement. Documented in the tuning UI/docs.

5. **Eval parity** — The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is brought
   to wrap-parity with the game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of
   being culled off-field, and hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped
   path (matching the seam-aware aim the enemy wrap epic ships), so eval scores
   measure wrap-aware play. `arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet and
   seam-aim cases.

6. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering
   (all four edges, raw vs. wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped
   nearest-selection when raw and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin
   retirement and eval parity. The human-like governor's reaction cadence,
   controls and thrust feel are unchanged (existing steering/bot integration
   tests stay green, plus new wrap scenarios). `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` are updated to describe the wrap-aware model. The full
   project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- One shared implementation in the bot decision layer — no divergent per-behaviour
  seam copies; share/adapt the seam maths the enemy wrap epic develops rather
  than reinventing.
- The human-like governor (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) is preserved: reaction
  cadence, W/A/D + optional reverse, seeded aim-skill noise and human-feel
  thrust presses are unchanged; wrap-awareness is a model property, not a
  scripted manœuvre.
- Use the seam when it is net-positive (Q2) — nearest-wrapped-path selection
  already yields that; no deliberate "wrap tricks".
- Do not change game physics (player/enemy/bullet wrap models); the bot's model
  must match the game, not alter it.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **Player wraps at all four edges** — `src/utils/movementModel.ts`
  (`if (x < 0) x += width; if (x >= width) x -= width;` and same for y). The
  headless eval arena drives the bot through the same `asteroidModel.tick(width,
  height)`, so the bot's own ship already wraps there.
- **Bullets wrap (game)** — `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` four-edge wrap;
  raider patrol wraps (`src/scenes/core/raiderPatrol.ts`). **Eval culls bullets
  off-field instead** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` `offField`), and hostile fire
  there aims at the raw player position.
- **Bot treats edges as walls** — legacy `botDecision.ts` `evaluateVector`
  ("a direction is unsafe when it reaches a wall within `wallMargin`") and
  competent `steering.ts` `evaluateDirection` (same); both tuned by a
  `wallMargin` knob (`botDecision.ts:189`, `competent/tunables.ts:239`,
  `style/fitting.ts`, `tuningFields.ts:94`).
- **All geometry is raw Euclidean** — `competent/goals.ts` `nearestTarget`
  (`Math.hypot`), `competent/steering.ts` `bearingTo` / `interceptPoint` /
  `closestApproach`, `worldModel.ts` `nearestEnemyDistance` /
  `predictIncomingFire`, `botDecision.ts` distance / closestApproach.
- **Existing wrap compensation, not awareness** — `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`
  deliberately clamps spurious position jumps caused by wrap/respawn.
- **Tests assert the bot never wraps** — `botSteering.integration.test.ts`
  ("it never wraps the screen").
- **Enemy wrap epic in flight** — AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 makes enemies wrap and fire
  across seams (blocked child slices AH-0MVKXBV0O005Q77P, AH-0MVKXBWDY008R0YH,
  AH-0MVKXBSAD003VRMF, AH-0MVKXBTNJ003F1TC, AH-0MVKXBXQX003S7K5,
  AH-0MVKXBZ5N007LKH4); once it lands, a wrap-blind bot fails to aim or dodge
  seam fire at all.

## Desired change

Give the bot's decision layer a single, shared wrap-aware (torus) model:

1. **Wrap-aware steering primitives** in the decision layer — a wrapped bearing /
   delta helper alongside the existing raw geometry, with a small hysteresis at
   nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths so targeting does not flip duplicates every
   tick; use it for the four steering/clearance tests (legacy + competent) and
   for `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint`.
2. **Wrapped nearest-selection** — `nearestTarget`, `nearestEnemyDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distances use wrapped distance; evade flees across a
   seam when that is the safest separation.
3. **Seam-aware prediction** — `predictIncomingFire` and the closest-approach
   solves run on the torus; verify `hazardVelocity` still clamps only true
   teleports.
4. **`wallMargin` retirement** — remove/re-purpose the knob and its style-fit
   mapping; keep saved configs loading.
5. **Eval parity** — wrap enemy bullets, aim hostile fire along the shortest
   wrapped path, and update `arena.test.ts` so metrics capture wrap-aware play.
6. **Docs & tests** — update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` / `docs/EVALUATION.md`; add
   the wrap-scenario tests from AC1–AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — wrap-aware `evaluateDirection`
  (no wall-margin wall test), `bearingTo`, `interceptPoint`, `closestApproach`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget` and goal distances on
  the wrapped torus.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `nearestEnemyDistance`, `predictIncomingFire`
  on the torus.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect/engage/evade distances
  and the evade flee direction.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — legacy `evaluateVector`, legacy aim/aim-delta and
  closest-approach paths.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts` — re-verify the wrap-jump clamp under the
  torus model; adjust only if double-compensating.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`,
  `src/ai/style/fitting.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`,
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — retire/re-purpose `wallMargin`; keep config
  loading tolerant.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` + `arena.test.ts` — wrapped enemy bullets, seam-aware
  hostile aim, parity tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` — describe the wrap-aware model.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`, plus a
  dedicated wrap-geometry unit test module.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** — "Enemies should be aware of the wrap around" (open
  epic with blocked child slices). Enemy counterpart: wrap-aware enemy movement
  and seam-aware enemy fire. Directly relevant — share the seam maths/helpers
  and sequence work so the bot and enemies land coherently.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed) — the wrap model the game's bullets use.
- **AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO** — "Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour
  tree, predictive dodge/aim" (completed) — the competent layer this change
  extends.
- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** — "Demo bot: human-like input limits" (completed) —
  the human-like governor whose look-and-feel must be preserved.
- **AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN** — "Predict enemy movement (bot)" (completed) — the
  hazard-velocity tracker whose wrap clamp interacts with the torus model.
- **AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV** — "Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay
  objects as the main game" (open) — bot/gym parity concern; watch for overlap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: duplicate flapping** — when the raw path and the wrapped path are
  nearly equal, a naive min-distance choice can flip between two seam
  duplicates every tick; mitigated with a small hysteresis/tolerance at near-equal
  lengths (the commitment layer already adds some hysteresis).
- **Risk: `wallMargin` migration ripple** — the knob appears across tunables,
  style-fitting, the tuning UI and saved `bot-tuning.json`; handle removal so
  saved configs keep loading, update the fit mapping, and document the behaviour
  change for old configs.
- **Risk: double-compensation** — `hazardVelocity` clamps wrap jumps today;
  once positions are modelled on the torus, verify the tracker only clamps true
  teleports/respawns and never swallows legitimate seam re-entry.
- **Risk: eval divergence** — the headless arena must mirror the game's wrap
  physics or wrap-aware behaviour earns no eval credit; keep the parity change
  minimal (bullet wrap + seam aim) and covered by `arena.test.ts`.
- **Scope-creep guard** — out of scope: game physics changes, non-torus
  pathfinding/routing, scripted wrap manœuvres, and any enemy/wrap changes
  beyond the arena-parity bump. Anything extra found becomes a linked work item,
  not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: dimensions** — the bot already receives playfield dimensions via
  tunables (`playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`, 960×540), so the torus needs no
  snapshot changes.
- **Assumption: seam maths reuse** — the enemy wrap epic (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8)
  will have developed wrapped-delta helpers; reuse/adapt rather than duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of wrap-awareness for the bot? (a) Movement/steering only. (b) +
  seam-aware aim/targeting. (c) Full torus model — plus seam-aware threat/hazard
  prediction." — Answer (Map): "(c) Full torus model". Source: producer reply on
  the work item (comment thread AH-C0MVR682R00022NOC). Research: steering walls
  in `botDecision.ts` + `steering.ts`, raw Euclidean geometry throughout
  (`goals.ts`, `worldModel.ts`, `behaviours.ts`), enemy wrap epic
  AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 in flight.
- Q2: "Should the bot deliberately *use* the seam as a manœuvre, or merely stop
  avoiding edges?" — Answer (Map): "Use it when net-positive". Source: producer
  reply on the work item. Research: nearest-wrapped-path selection yields
  net-positive seam use naturally; no scripted trick, human-like governor
  unchanged.
- Q3: "Should the headless eval arena be brought to wrap-parity with the game so
  eval measures wrap-aware play?" — Answer (Map): "Yes". Source: producer reply
  on the work item. Research: `arena.ts` culls enemy bullets off-field and aims
  hostile fire at the raw player position — both diverge from the game.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** – Enemies should be aware of the wrap around (open)
- **AH-0MU8FOQ7L005AII0** – Core Asteroid Entity + Unit Tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap

# Intake brief — Arc weapon should not affect asteroids

> **Status:** intake draft produced without an interactive producer (the item was
> auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker). Scope is derived from the
> operator's seed intent and from the code/design docs; one scope question is
> recorded in the Appendix with a recommended default so planning is not
> blocked.

## Problem statement

The **Arc** weapon is the only auto-targeting area-of-effect weapon: every beat
(750 ms) it strikes the target nearest the ship and chains to two more within
60 px. Its target list is the raw enemy list, which also carries the inert
`asteroid` world hazard — so the bolt silently spends itself on rock: it
shatters asteroids the player never aimed at, and every destroyed small rock
pays a mineral plus a roll at the rare **Extra Life** drop. In play this reads
both as "the weapon is doing the wrong thing" and as "the weapon is too
powerful", because Arc farms the asteroid economy automatically instead of
fighting the enemies it is aimed at.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the Arc bolt to hit ships, not waste its chain on drifting
  rock.
  - *As a player, I want the Arc to strike the nearest **enemy** even when a
    rock is closer, so my timed weapon is spent on threats.*
  - *As a player, I do not want a weapon to farm minerals and Extra Lives off
    asteroids I did not shoot, because that makes the pickup overpowered and
    the reward feel unearned.*
- **Producer / designer** — wants one stated rule for player auto-targeting
  offence that matches the already-shipped Orbital Strike fix
  (AH-0MVU3341U001B40T): auto-targeting weapons pick enemies, inert world
  hazards are not targets.
  - *As a designer, I want the rule written down and pinned by tests so a
    future AOE weapon cannot silently regress into "fires on asteroids".*
- **Agent / gym user** — the game and every gym must run the identical rule
  (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1), so the change must live in the shared
  core/helpers, never in a per-scene copy.

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Arc definition:** `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.arc.aoe` =
  `{ trigger: 'onFire', radius: 60, damagesEnemies: true,
  clearsEnemyBullets: true, chains: 2 }` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, Arc entry
  around line 1240; radius in `AOE_RADII.arc`). Its catalogue description
  already promises "strikes the nearest enemy".
- **Dispatch:** `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` calls `onAoeFired` for `onFire`
  effects; `CombatScene.onAoeFired` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:709`)
  builds the chain with
  `selectChainTargets(x, y, this.getEnemyEntities(), aoe.chains + 1, aoe.radius)`
  and then applies damage, the along-path bullet clear, the bolt VFX and the
  impact feedback from that one selection.
- **Target selection:** `selectChainTargets`/`findNearestTarget`
  (`src/utils/aoe.ts:150` / `:172`) filter only `alive === false`. There is no
  target-kind filter of any sort.
- **Enemy list contents:** `PlayScene.getEnemyEntities()` returns every spawned
  entity (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3702`), asteroids included. `Asteroid`
  reports `archetype === 'asteroid'` (`src/entities/Asteroid.ts:274`).
- **Precedent — Orbital Strike:** the same class of bug was fixed for the
  Orbital Strike by `selectOrbitalStrikeTarget` +
  `ORBITAL_STRIKE_EXCLUDED_ARCHETYPES = ['asteroid']`
  (`src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`, AH-0MVU3341U001B40T). That module
  explicitly notes "every other weapon may still hit asteroids", so Arc is the
  remaining offender among the auto-targeting offence.
- **Why "too powerful":** a destroyed **small** asteroid drops exactly one
  mineral (`scatterMineralDrops`/`mineralKillDrops.ts`) and additionally rolls
  the configurable Extra Life chance (`src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`),
  while large/medium rocks split. An every-beat auto-chain is therefore a
  mineral/Extra-Life farm that needs no aim.
- **Gym parity:** the shared dispatch means gyms inherit the fix. `GymWeapons`
  demonstrates the Arc against inert `TrainingTarget`s that have **no**
  `archetype` (documented gym-only divergence), and `GymFormationScene`/
  `GymLevel` spawn Arc drops alongside the asteroid hazard — so the rule must
  treat an absent archetype as "ordinary enemy" (targetable).

## Desired change

Arc's chain selection considers only live targets that are **not** inert world
hazards:

1. The primary target is the nearest **eligible enemy**, even when an asteroid
   is nearer to the ship.
2. Chain hops also skip asteroids, so a chain can step across/around a rock
   from enemy to enemy (rocks neither absorb a hop nor break the chain).
3. The bolt VFX, the impact flashes and the along-path bullet clear are
   derived from the same eligible chain, so they never show a segment to a
   rock.
4. A field holding **only** asteroids behaves exactly like today's empty
   field: no damage, no chain VFX, no impact cue (the existing "Arc is a no-op
   with no live enemies" behaviour).
5. Nova, Mortar and the Smart Bomb pulse are **unchanged** — they may still hit
   asteroids (see Assumption A1 and the Appendix question).
6. The rule is implemented once in a shared, pure helper consumed by the shared
   combat core, so the game and every gym cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Arc never targets, damages or destroys an asteroid.** With an
  asteroid nearer the ship than a ship enemy, firing Arc strikes the enemy and
  leaves the asteroid `alive`; with an enemy–asteroid–enemy line inside the
  chain reach, both enemies take damage and the asteroid takes none (pinned by
  scene-level tests in `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` plus a pure-helper
  test).
- **AC2 — Chain hops skip asteroids without breaking the chain.** A chain whose
  geometrically nearest next hop is a rock continues to the next eligible enemy
  up to the unchanged link budget (`chains: 2` → primary + 2 hops) and within
  the unchanged 60 px reach.
- **AC3 — A field containing only asteroids is a no-op.** Firing Arc with no
  eligible enemy damages nothing, spawns no chain VFX, plays no impact cue and
  performs no asteroid kill accounting (no minerals, no Extra Life roll) —
  identical to the existing empty-field behaviour.
- **AC4 — The rule is defined once and shared.** Target eligibility is decided
  by one pure helper/module in `src/` (no per-scene copy); `CombatScene` and the
  gym-owned AOE demos consume it, the `GymWeapons` training targets (no
  `archetype`) remain targetable, and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`
  (the duplicate-body guard) still passes.
- **AC5 — Unchanged weapons stay unchanged (regression pin).** Nova, Mortar and
  the Smart Bomb pulse still damage asteroids inside their areas, and the cannon
  still destroys an asteroid on contact — asserted by regression tests so a
  future change cannot widen the exclusion silently.
- **AC6 — Asteroid and wave accounting are untouched.** Arc kills award
  exactly what they awarded before for enemy ships (score/drop/wave advance
  unchanged); destroying an asteroid by other means still yields its mineral
  and Extra Life roll.
- **AC7 — At least one new automated test covers each behaviour above**, and
  the changed-scope gate (`/skill:test` changed scope) passes.
- **AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.** (GDD §4.4 A3 table row and the AOE-appendix paragraph,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` AOE section, plus JSDoc on the
  helper and on `selectChainTargets`.)
- **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Shared core only.** The behaviour must live in the shared pure helper +
  `CombatScene.onAoeFired` path; no per-scene copies (the duplicate-body guard
  and gym↔game parity rule).
- **Identify hazards by archetype string, not by class.** The game's
  `EnemyEntity` and the gym's `FormationSceneEntity` must classify identically;
  `instanceof Asteroid` would break gym parity and stub harnesses.
- **Absent archetype = targetable.** Historical stubs, `TrainingTarget`s and
  entities without an archetype must keep working (only an explicit inert-hazard
  key is excluded).
- **No tuning changes.** Fire rate (1 beat), radius (60 px) and chain count
  (2) stay exactly as shipped; this is a targeting fix, not a nerf knob.
- **Deterministic selection.** Existing tie-breaking (earlier candidate wins)
  and hop order must be preserved so the result is reproducible.
- **No new player-facing UI/text** beyond the already-correct catalogue
  description; no new config option unless the implementation needs one (drop
  weights, power-up catalogue and HUD are untouched).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/aoe.ts` — `selectChainTargets`/`findNearestTarget` gain an
  eligibility filter (or a sibling helper does the filtering); keep them pure
  and unit-tested.
- `src/utils/aoe.test.ts` — pure-helper tests for asteroid-skipping, chain
  continuation and reach limits.
- `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts` — likely home for a shared
  "inert world hazard / not an auto-target" rule (or factor the exclusion list
  into a small shared module both Arc and Orbital Strike consume).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — pass the eligibility rule from
  `onAoeFired` so the chain, VFX, bullet clear and impact feedback all use the
  filtered chain.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` — Arc-never-hits-asteroids behaviour,
  only-rocks-is-a-no-op, and the unchanged Nova/Mortar/Smart Bomb regressions.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity guard check after
  the change.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 table row A3 and the AOE weapons
  appendix paragraph (state "strikes the nearest **enemy**; asteroids are not
  targets").
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — AOE dispatch section that lists
  Asteroids as world hazards (near the Arc/Orbital Strike notes).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — Arc becomes a no-op beat in asteroid-heavy waves.** With no eligible
  enemy the bolt vanishes (by design, matching today's empty field) while the
  timer still runs. Mitigation: verify in `GymLevel`/`GymWeapons` that the
  silent beat reads acceptably; if it does not, a follow-up item (not scope
  creep here) can add a "bolt fizzles" cue.
- **Risk — over-broad exclusion.** `isNonBlockingHazard` also classifies
  `lane-traffic`; excluding lane traffic as well would be a silent behaviour
  change beyond the item's wording (and contradicts Orbital Strike, which keeps
  lane traffic targetable). Mitigation: exclude only the inert rock hazard;
  record any widening as a separate decision.
- **Risk — gym demos regress.** A filter requiring an `archetype` would break
  the `GymWeapons` training targets. Mitigation: absent archetype stays
  targetable; AC4 pins it.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Widening the rule to Nova/Mortar/Smart Bomb, or
  re-tuning Arc's power budget, is a separate balance decision — record as
  linked work items rather than folding into this fix.
- **Assumption A1 — scope is the Arc weapon only.** Nova, Mortar and the Smart
  Bomb keep damaging asteroids, matching the item title and the Orbital Strike
  precedent note that "every other weapon may still hit asteroids". Confirm at
  review (see Appendix Q1).
- **Assumption A2 — "only enemies" means inert world hazards are excluded, not
  that every non-asteroid hazard is.** Lane traffic remains a valid target.
- **Assumption A3 — no scoring/currency change is required.** Removing the
  accidental asteroid farm is the intended effect; asteroid rewards via aimed
  fire are untouched.
- **Assumption A4 — no new player-facing text is needed** because the catalogue
  description already says "strikes the nearest enemy"; only docs/JSDoc need
  aligning.

## Related work

- Orbital Strike must not target asteroids (producer rejection remediation)
  (AH-0MVU3341U001B40T) — **direct precedent**: the same "auto-targeting must
  pick enemies, not rock" fix, with the shared `strikeTargeting.ts` rule this
  item should align with (or share).
- Orbital Strike does nothing (AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V) — the producer rejection
  that produced the precedent ("Stop it firing on asteroids, we want it to fire
  on the nearest enemy").
- Asteroids drop more lives (AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S) — explains the Extra Life
  reward that makes the Arc asteroid farm overpowered.
- Asteroids as an enemy (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) — why asteroids appear in the
  shared enemy list at all.
- New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4) —
  origin of the Arc weapon (AOE family, parent AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD).
- Weapon upgrades are too powerful (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T) — adjacent balance
  work; not blocking and **not** a duplicate (it rebalances damage/upgrade
  curves, not targeting).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

> This intake was auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker, so no
> interactive producer was present. Questions are recorded here with the
> agent's recommended option and the assumption applied to the draft; none of
> them blocks drafting, planning or implementation. Each is mirrored in a
> work-item comment so the producer can redirect at review time.

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review) — Does "should not affect
  asteroids" apply to the other area-of-effect weapons too?**
  - *A. Arc only.* Nova (ship-centred ring), Mortar (random blast) and the
    Smart Bomb pulse keep damaging asteroids; only the auto-targeting chain is
    fixed. This matches the item title and the Orbital Strike precedent
    ("every other weapon may still hit asteroids").
  - *B. All AOE weapons.* Nova/Mortar/Smart Bomb also stop affecting
    asteroids.
  - *C. Arc + all auto-targeting offence.* Arc only today (Orbital Strike
    already fixed), plus a documented standing rule for future auto-targeting
    weapons.
  - **Recommended: A (+ the standing-rule wording from C in the docs)** — the
    reported problem is the automatic, aim-free chain; Nova/Mortar require the
    player to close on or aim near a rock, which is legitimate play. A wider
    change would alter balance well beyond the report.
  - *Answer:* **Not answered — no interactive producer.** Draft applies option
    A (Assumption A1) so planning is not blocked.
  - *Evidence:* `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts` header ("every other
    weapon may still hit asteroids"), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 A3
    ("Strikes the nearest enemy …"), `src/utils/weapons.ts` Arc catalogue
    description.

- **Q2 (RESOLVED by research) — Which entity key marks rock, and can it be
  read without coupling the rule to a class?**
  - *Answer (agent, repo research):* `Asteroid.archetype` returns `'asteroid'`
    (`src/entities/Asteroid.ts:274`) and `BaseEnemy.archetype` exposes the
    default `'unknown'` for others (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:521`); the
    Orbital Strike rule already excludes by string
    (`ORBITAL_STRIKE_EXCLUDED_ARCHETYPES`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`).
    Entities with no archetype at all (`GymWeapons` `TrainingTarget`s) must stay
    targetable. *Source:* file inspection, 2026-10-30.

- **Q3 (RESOLVED by research) — Is there a documented reason Arc hits rock
  today?**
  - *Answer (agent, repo research):* no. All AOE weapons share one target list
    (`getEnemyEntities()` includes asteroids); nothing in the GDD, the AOE
    appendix or the code comments intends Arc to strike rock. The only recorded
    intent is the catalogue text "strikes the nearest enemy". *Source:*
    `src/utils/weapons.ts` (Arc), `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:709`,
    `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 A3.

- **Duplicate-work check** — `wl search "arc weapon asteroid"`,
  `wl search "asteroid"`, `wl search "too powerful"` and
  `wl search "chaining bolt asteroid"` were run. The nearest items are
  precedents, not duplicates: Orbital Strike must not target asteroids
  (AH-0MVU3341U001B40T) — fixed for a *different* weapon and explicitly leaves
  other weapons free to hit asteroids; Orbital Strike does nothing
  (AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V) — its parent report; Weapon upgrades are too powerful
  (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T) — a damage/upgrade-curve rebalance that does not change
  targeting; Asteroids drop more lives (AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S) — the reward rule
  that makes this bug significant, not a fix for it. **No overlapping completed
  item found.**

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVU3341U001B40T** – Orbital Strike must not target asteroids (producer rejection remediation) (completed)
- **AH-0MU8FORFF005RD9M** – PlayScene Integration + Unit Tests (completed)
